=== FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===
- .github/workflows/orchestrate_poll.yml:833-834 | severity=NIT | confidence=2
  PROBLEM: The outer `any(.[]; ...)` evaluates to true when ANY issue in the listing passes the filter. This is correct preflight semantics: the pool should be fetched when any eligible Claude-labeled standalone issue exists, and the per-issue judge then resolves its own engine. The filter correctly excludes `ai:codex` issues and tracking issues. The 1000-result cap matches the existing limit in `run_standalone_stall_recovery` (scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:17456). No logic defect.
  WHY: Does not fail. The preflight correctly decides whether to fetch the Claude pool.
- .github/workflows/orchestrate_poll.yml:831 (`gh issue list --limit 1000`) | severity=NIT | confidence=2
  PROBLEM: The `gh issue list --limit 1000` read-only call is guarded: it runs only when (a) `any_claude` is still false after the tracking-label check, (b) both `ENABLE_STANDALONE_STALL_RECOVERY` and `ENABLE_STALL_JUDGE` are enabled, and (c) the STALL_JUDGE default is not Claude. The comment at lines 817-827 already audits the API cost against the existing batched GraphQL caches and notes this path is never hit in the default configuration. The 1000-result limit matches `run_standalone_stall_recovery`'s existing per-label scan. No new performance regression.
  WHY: Does not fail. The call is correctly gated and bounded.
- .github/workflows/orchestrate_poll.yml:768-771 (`GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GH_PAT }}`, `ENABLE_STANDALONE_STALL_RECOVERY`, `ENABLE_STALL_JUDGE`) | severity=NIT | confidence=2
  PROBLEM: The step now exposes `GH_TOKEN` from `GH_PAT` for a single read-only `gh issue list` call. The same step already runs with the Actions runner's `GITHUB_TOKEN`. The broader PAT is used only for this one listing call, which needs to read issue labels. The call is scoped to the local repository via `--repo "${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}"`. The two new feature-flag env vars (`ENABLE_STANDALONE_STALL_RECOVERY`, `ENABLE_STALL_JUDGE`) gate the entire standalone check path and both default to `true`, matching the existing poller defaults. The standalone path is further gated by `any_claude != "true"` so it never overrides an existing tracking-based Claude decision.
  WHY: Does not fail. The token exposure is limited to one read-only API call in a bounded code path.
=== END FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===

=== FINDINGS FROM openai_gpt-6-luna ===
- .github/workflows/orchestrate_poll.yml:Line 831; scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh lines 17454-17457 and 18050 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The Claude-labelled issue preflight scan is capped at 1,000 results, independently of the phase-label scans that select standalone recovery candidates.
  WHY: An eligible issue can fall outside the first 1,000 `ai:engine-claude` results but within the first 1,000 results for its phase label. The recovery scan then finds it and passes its Claude label to the judge, while this preflight leaves `any_claude=false` and does not fetch the Claude pool.
- .github/workflows/ci.yml:Lines 1429-1442 | severity=BLOCKER | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The supplied CI results show `orchestrate-poll (3)` failed and the aggregate `lint` check failed. The available log tail reports 33 passing tests and one failed shard, but does not identify the failing shard result or cause.
  WHY: The CI step fails when a shard has a nonzero or missing exit status. This PR head therefore has not passed CI; the shard failure needs investigation before validation is complete.
=== END FINDINGS FROM openai_gpt-6-luna ===

=== FINDINGS FROM qwen_qwen3_7-plus ===
- .github/workflows/orchestrate_poll.yml:Line 831 (`--limit 1000` in the `gh issue list` call) | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The preflight caps its `ai:engine-claude` scan at 1,000 results, but `run_standalone_stall_recovery` gathers candidates via separate phase-label scans (scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:17454-17457). When more than 1,000 open issues carry `ai:engine-claude`, the preflight can miss an eligible issue that a phase-label scan would select.
  WHY: If an issue beyond the 1,000-result cap has `ai:engine-claude` (and not `ai:codex` or `ai:orchestrator-tracking`), the preflight sets `any_claude=false`. The standalone stall judge then selects Claude from that issue's labels, but the Claude CLI and account pool were never installed/fetched, so the judge falls back to the sandboxed OpenCode path. The comment at line 828-829 claims "every issue it can select is covered," but that is only true when the total number of `ai:engine-claude` issues is at most 1,000.
- .github/workflows/ci.yml (aggregate `lint` job):PR check run `orchestrate-poll (3)` on head `58ac3922e43473caa6509c4b5c0f5b84d93e70a6`, job log lines 1431-1441 | severity=BLOCKER | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The CI shard `orchestrate-poll (3)` reports "33 passed, 0 failed, 33 total" but then exits with "1 orchestrate-poll shard(s) failed." The aggregate `lint` check fails as a result. The captured log tail does not identify the cause of the shard failure.
  WHY: The CI harness treats a nonzero or missing shard exit status as failure. The PR's CI remains red, so the change cannot be validated or merged until the shard failure is investigated and resolved.
=== END FINDINGS FROM qwen_qwen3_7-plus ===
